chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman, entered into her (consummated the marriage), but did not specify a dowry for her. Then he divorced her. He said to her: 'She is entitled to the dowry of her equals, and he must provide her with mut'ah (consolation gift).'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He entered into her (consummated the marriage)
key_terms.لَمْ يُفْرِضْ لَهَا: He did not specify/fix for her
key_terms.مَهْرُ مِثْلِ: Dowry of her equals (standard dowry for women of similar status)
key_terms.يُمَتِّعُهَا: He provides her with mut'ah (consolation gift)

ai.seo_question: What is the dowry entitlement for a woman if her husband divorces her after consummation without having specified a fixed dowry?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the default financial rights in a marriage where the specific dowry was omitted prior to consummation, establishing 'mahr al-mithl' as the standard compensation. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the act of entering the marital chamber triggers these financial obligations even in the absence of a prior agreement, ensuring the wife's economic security upon divorce.
